Evidence: runs-repository treats errorCode as sticky: options.errorCode === undefined leaves the stored code, null clears (comment runs-repository.ts:126-129, pinned by tests 'preserves a stored errorCode' / 'clears errorCode only on explicit null'). state-gate.ts:28 passes input.errorCode ?? null, so an omitted errorCode becomes an explicit null -> the gate clears a stored failure code on every reason-only hop. Fixed 2026-10-07 (fix-state-micro-002-003): the gate passes input.errorCode through unchanged (undefined = preserve stored code, null = explicit clear); pinned by src/state/state-gate.test.ts.
Reproduction: Transition a run to failed with errorCode E_BOOT; later applyRunTransition({to:'resumable'|...}) with no errorCode; the stored code becomes null although the executor passed no clear intent.
Root cause: The gate normalizes undefined to null at the boundary, inverting the callee's documented sticky semantics.
Impact: Last failure code erased by recovery hops routed through the gate; diagnostics lose the root error for exactly the executor paths the gate owns.
Proposed fix: Pass input.errorCode through unchanged (undefined stays undefined); keep null as the explicit clear. One-line change, same wire shape.
Required tests: Unit test mirroring RUN-001 through the gate: reason-only hop preserves stored code; explicit null clears.

Evidence: applyMessage has zero callers (grep repo-wide: only its own definition and stateGate object). The execution-path message writer runtime-kernel.ts:198 calls messageGate.append directly with { broker }; the gate comment (:60-61) admits it is a passthrough. State.md 'Architectural Standard (Target)' claims 'All message commits from execution paths go through stateGate.applyMessage (or messageGate.append where the gate alias is threaded)'.
Reproduction: grep -R 'applyMessage' packages/server/src -> only state-gate.ts. No runtime call site routes through it.
Root cause: The port was created as a placeholder for symmetry and never adopted; the doc's two-way wording keeps it ambiguous.
Impact: Dead export inflates the gate contract (docs must maintain it); no functional harm today, but 'one entry point per entity type' is fiction.
Proposed fix: Either wire runtime-kernel/swarm/scheduler message writes through applyMessage, or remove the port and re-word State.md to name messageGate.append as the single message entry point.
Required tests: Import-graph check after either decision; doc Ports equals gate exports.

Evidence: Persist (await runsGate.transition) happens before emit; the emit block swallows all failures with console.error (:53-55) and the missing-broker case only warns (:35-36). No outbox, retry, or reconciliation exists: the event log subscriber (create-app.ts:365 eventsGate.recordDetached) only records events that were actually emitted, and orphan-sweep/resumeRun have the same shape.
Reproduction: Kill/restart the API between the runs UPDATE commit and the broker emit (or run an executor in a context with no shared broker registered): the row shows the new status, no run.status_changed was emitted, and nothing replays it.
Root cause: Persist-then-emit with no compensation on the emit leg; the transition outcome is returned as success regardless.
Impact: Clients and the durable event log permanently miss a status change; status views drift from the runs table until a full snapshot read.
Proposed fix: Emit-after-persist is acceptable, but add a replay/repair leg (e.g. emit from the sweep/snapshot path by comparing rows, or outbox the event in the same transaction as the status write).
Required tests: Failure-injection test: broker throwing/no-broker leaves the row changed and the gap is repaired by the chosen mechanism.
Status: Fixed-verified 2026-10-07 (fix-state-micro-005-007): repair leg added - missing broker/emit-throw buffers latest payload per run (cap 500, latest-wins) and flushPendingStatusEvents() re-emits; wired via stateGate (state-gate.ts:51-111); tests src/state/state-gate.test.ts; evidence: npx vitest run src/state 12 passed, npx tsc exit 0; residual: durable repair across hard kills (Runs sweep/outbox) remains open

Evidence: The run.status_changed payload is hand-built in three places with identical keys but independent casts (runs-service and orphan-sweep cast through 'as never'; state-gate uses typed fields). EventBrokerMap pins the key set once (event-types.ts:36-47) but nothing links the three builders.
Reproduction: Add a payload field in one emitter (or rename one) and the other two silently drift; consumers see shape-dependent events.
Root cause: No shared builder for a wire contract with three producers.
Impact: Silent event-schema drift across paths; redaction/logging/consumers cannot assume one shape from one producer.
Proposed fix: Extract one buildRunStatusChangedPayload(row, from, to, reason) helper (e.g. in runs) and use it from all three emitters.
Required tests: Type-level: each emitter's output assignable to RunStatusChangedEventPayload; runtime shape test comparing the three paths.

Evidence: Both exported functions have inferred return types (applyRunTransition -> Promise<TransitionResult | null>; applyMessage -> messages row). No explicit annotations, so a callee type change silently widens/narrows the gate contract; also applyMessage's opts default ({}) hides whether broker/tx are threaded.
Reproduction: Change messageGate.append's return type; state-gate.ts still compiles and callers see the new type without a contract review.
Root cause: Inferred-only public surface on a facade whose contract is docs-managed.
Impact: Contract drift is invisible in diffs; doc 'Ports' cannot be mechanically checked against types.
Proposed fix: Add explicit return annotations matching the documented contract.
